Boldog születésnapot, Magyarország!” – posztolta Orbán Viktor volt miniszterelnök augusztus 20-án a Facebook-oldalán . A Fidesz elnöke a bejegyzésben a Kiss Kata Zenekar Megmaradni magyarnak című számával osztotta meg a köszöntést. „A falak megőrzik azoknak a hangját, akik előttünk éltek, és továbbadják azoknak, akik utánunk érkeznek”, áll a megosztott videó elején. Orbán kommentelt is a bejegyzés alá: „Gyönyörű dal lett, köszönjük!”, írta. Orbán Viktor utoljára július 27-én szólalt meg a Facebook-oldalán, az elmúlt hetek víz- és áramkrízisértől egyszer sem szólalt fel a legnagyobb ellenzéki párt vezetőjeként. Egy olvasónk néhány napja Abbázia utcáin fotózta le a volt miniszterelnököt, Rogán Antal és Schmidt Mária társaságában. Orbán néhány órával azután posztolt, hogy csütörtök reggel a Fidesz egyik fő politikusa, Navracsics Tibor bejelentette, párbeszédet kezdeményezne párthovatartozástól függetlenül mindenkivel . A volt közigazgatási és területfejlesztési miniszter Magyarország jövőjéről és múltjáról tervez beszélgetni, mert „két oldal helyett egyenes út kell”. Havasi Bertalan, a Fidesz kommunikációs igazgatója erre azt reagálta, neki a Fidesz az egyenes út , Magyar Péter miniszterelnökkel lehetetlen párbeszédet folytatni. https://www.webwire.com/ViewPressRel.asp.text: Deliver Your News to the World Home News How We Work Compare Services FAQ All WebPost WebRelease Targeted Media Wire Service BGK and EIF invest 30 million in new Inovo fund under Future Tech Poland programme Fourth investment signed under the Future Tech Poland initiative managed by the EIF and backed by BGK 30 million commitment to new Inovo fund supporting early-stage technology companies PLN 580 million already allocated under Future Tech Poland Investment to strengthen Polands venture capital ecosystem and support innovative high-growth businesses The European Investment Fund (EIF) and Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego (BGK) have invested 30 million (approximately PLN 129 million) in a new venture capital fund managed by Inovo.vc . This is the fourth investment backed by both institutions under their joint initiative, Future Tech Poland (FTP). To date, FTP has allocated around PLN 580 million. Inovo.vc invests in early-stage technology companies. Future Tech Polands commitment to Inovo.vc s new fund reflects its objective of supporting venture capital managers that back innovative, high-growth companies. The value of FTPs investment in the new fund, including EIFs co-investment, amounts to 30 million, or approximately PLN 129 million. Our investment in Inovo builds on that objective, supporting a proven team that helps ambitious technology companies grow from an early stage and develop solutions with the potential to compete across Europe and globally, said Marjut Falkstedt, Chief Executive of the European Investment Fund. The investment in the fund managed by Inovo.vc is already the fourth transaction under the Future Tech Poland programme, which is one of the pillars of the Innovate Poland initiative. It also marks another step in the implementation of BGKs investment strategy. Our goal is to systematically strengthen Polands competitiveness and consistently reinforce the domestic venture capital ecosystem, ensuring that institutional capital reaches the countrys most innovative companies. By the end of the year, we plan to achieve more than 40% of the total allocation of Future Tech Poland funds, said Jarosław Dąbrowski, Member of the Management Board of BGK. Since 2014, Inovo.vc has backed the most ambitious founders building early-stage technology companies across Poland and Central and Eastern Europe  over that time weve supported more than 70 teams. We believe the next generation of global technology leaders will come from Poland and the region. Our role is to be their first institutional partner and support them on their way to becoming global leaders in their categories. Were proud to pursue that mission together with BGK and the EIF through Future Tech Poland  their involvement genuinely matters for the development of this market, said Tomasz Swieboda, Managing Partner, Inovo.vc . Future Tech Poland is a joint initiative of BGK and the EIF and one of the pillars of the Innovate Poland programme. FTP operates as a fund-of-funds managed by the EIF, with a PLN 1bn allocation from BGK and a PLN 500m co-investment alongside the BGK allocation. The initiative aims to strengthen the Polish VC fund ecosystem, particularly by increasing the sizes of local funds, and to stimulate investment in Polish companies. Through its capital commitments, FTP supports innovation and growth in areas such as artificial intelligence, fintech, cybersecurity and defence technologies. About the European Investment Fund The European Investment Fund (EIF) is the subsidiary of the European Investment Bank Group specialised in providing guarantees and equity to improve access to finance for small and medium-sized businesses and startups across Europe. Acting as an anchor investor, through its extensive network of partnering banks and investment funds, the EIF mobilises private investment and nurtures the ecosystem of venture capital funds to support innovative European entrepreneurs. In 2023, the EIF together with six EU member states (France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Belgium and the Netherlands) launched the European Tech Champions Initiative, a fund-of-funds to scale up innovative startups. To date, this initiative has already enabled the creation of 14 European venture capital mega-funds and scaled up 40 companies, including 11 unicorns (with more than 1 billion in capital). The EIF has invested 8 billion in Poland to date, helping leverage some 25.8 billion in support for over 119,000 SMEs. About BGK Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego (BGK) is Polands development bank, supporting the countrys sustainable socio-economic growth. BGK implements strategic infrastructure projects, fosters innovation, and supports the development of Polish businesses both domestically and internationally. The bank cooperates with the European Investment Fund on equity investments, including through the Polish Growth Fund of Funds (PGFF) and the Three Seas Initiative Innovation Fund, which continues the mission of PGFF. Photograph: Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters Ukraine US gave us no warning of Russian strikes on Kyiv power plants, Zelenskyy says Ukrainian president accuses Washington of ‘denial of reality’ in ongoing row with Trump over apparent support for Moscow Andrew Roth in Kyiv Mon 19 Oct 2026 05.03 EDT Last modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 05.48 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Ukraine did not receive a warning from the US about an impending Russian missile attack on Sunday evening, Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said, reviving concerns that Washington is withholding intelligence in order to bully Kyiv into capitulating to Moscow. Yuri Ihnat, a spokesperson for the Ukrainian Air Force, said on television on Monday morning that Ukraine had not received a warning before a Russian missile barrage hit power plants in Kyiv at around 11pm. Earlier, a Ukrainian government official had told the Guardian the US had not warned the capital about the impending missile strike. Ukraine did receive a warning before a successive strike, at 3am, Ihnat added. “Once again, Russia launched a ballistic missile attack in multiple waves throughout the night, and once again, there was no warning from our partners,” Zelenskyy wrote in a social media post on Monday morning. “When the supply of missiles for Ukrainian air defence is blocked, and Russia receives sanctions relief or delays, it is, unfortunately, a denial of reality on the part of our partners,” the president added. On Friday, Donald Trump waived a sweeping package of sanctions on Russia , telling Congress the pause on the legislation, named after the late senator Lindsey Graham and passed by both chambers, was in the national interest. Ukraine has also complained of slowed deliveries of PAC-3 air defence missiles from the US. The US president wrote on Truth Social on Sunday: “My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table. “Zelenskyy doesn’t care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him … he doesn’t want to end this war , and probably never did.” For years, the US had warned Ukraine before Russia launches ballistic missiles, giving authorities several minutes to sound alarms and allow civilians to reach shelters before the strikes hit. However, Ukraine has said it was not warned on at least three days in the past week before missiles were launched, amid a public quarrel between Zelenskyy and Trump. Speaking in the early hours of Monday on a trip to Samarkand, Uzbekistan, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said: “If it happened last night, I don’t know exactly. I know a few nights ago there was a software problem involving their early warning system.” US officials have not previously mentioned a software glitch in the early warning system. In at least one case, Ukrainian officials had been told that bad weather over southern Russia had obscured preparations for the missile launch. Rubio said the military’s European Command was looking into the strikes. The US has maintained plausible deniability as services and programmes provided to support Ukraine have suddenly begun to fail. The Trump administration has denied that it throttled services in Ukraine for Starlink , the satellite internet service run by Elon Musk that is used both on offensive drones and anti-air weapons by Ukraine. Ukraine has also said US weapons delivered through the PURL scheme, where Europe purchases US weapons then delivers them to Ukraine, have been delayed. The Trump administration reportedly threatened Kyiv with a slowdown in crucial weapons deliveries unless it stopped striking Russian oil refineries.
